content: Ticketing is tiered and transparent on the event site: a Standard pass listed at $29, a Business pass at $199, and a VIP pass at $399, each marked down from higher list prices, with the VIP tier adding lounge access, reserved seating, and VIP lunch arrangements. All tiers include two-day exhibition and conference access plus the official app, and the site shows inventory counters for each category, worth monitoring if a particular tier is nearly gone.

Doors run 09:00 to 18:00 both days, November 26 and 27, which conveniently brackets the UAE weekend for local attendees. Abu Dhabi in late November is genuinely pleasant, roughly twenty-five degrees and dry, so budget energy for the evening circuit; the event's own materials note that most business happens after hours.

premier-ethwomen.summaryLead: ETHWomen Florida 2026 celebrates and accelerates women building in Ethereum and web3 with a one-day program in Miami on November 18, 2026, running alongside the Futurist Conference, North America's long-running traveling blockchain production.

sections.heading: A focused day inside a bigger production
content: ETHWomen occupies a deliberate niche: not a women's panel tucked into someone else's agenda, but a dedicated event built around women who ship in the Ethereum ecosystem. The November 18 date in Miami puts it alongside the Florida edition of the Futurist Conference, meaning attendees get a focused community day with a full-scale conference running next door.

The parent production brings serious institutional weight. Futurist was founded by Untraceable Events, Canada's first blockchain events company, producing large-scale crypto conferences since 2013, and was later acquired by Emerald, America's largest producer of B2B trade shows. Nine years in, the franchise splits its time between Toronto and Florida, and ETHWomen has grown up as one of its signature experience programs, linked prominently across the Futurist site.

sections.heading: The Futurist machinery behind it
content: The Futurist format is unorthodox on purpose. Instead of a convention-center grid, the conference stages outdoor cabanas, immersive installations, and networking-first layouts designed for deal flow, a philosophy its organizers describe as built for business development rather than badge scans. Across its editions the production claims 250-plus speakers, more than 150 web3 community partners, and over 120 media partners.

ETHWomen plugs directly into that apparatus. The broader Futurist ecosystem includes beginner bootcamps led by experts, hackathons such as ETH Toronto, NFT galleries, investor showcase programs with free or discounted VIP passes, and a gamified event experience running on its UNNY token. An ETHWomen attendee can move from a targeted community session into the wider conference floor without ever changing buildings.

sections.heading: Why Miami in mid-November
content: Timing and location do half the work. Mid-November in Miami means dry heat instead of summer swelter, and the city's crypto gravity has held since its post-2021 boom years, with local VCs, exchanges, and LatAm-facing businesses keeping the scene dense. Running in parallel with Futurist Florida means the usual conference-week dynamics apply: side events, evening gatherings, and a visitor base skewed toward people actively hiring and funding.

For international attendees, Miami remains one of the easiest US crypto destinations to reach, with MIA's route network covering Europe and Latin America directly. Book accommodation early regardless; conference weeks compress hotel availability across the whole downtown corridor, not just near the venue.

sections.heading: Making the case to attend
content: The honest argument for ETHWomen is compounding access. Women-led projects still raise a fraction of comparable crypto funding, and rooms where founders, engineers, and investors share a table on equal footing remain scarce enough to matter. An event that combines that access with the hiring surface and sponsor floor of a major conference offers more per hour than attending either alone.

There is also the mentorship economy around it. Programs of this kind historically pair emerging builders with senior engineers and founders for structured sessions, and the relationships formed there tend to outlast the event calendar by years. For teams weighing whether to send junior staff, that alone usually justifies the badge.

Check both ethwomen.com and futuristconference.com as November approaches for the confirmed venue, ticketing, and speaker announcements, since programming details firm up closest to the date. Students and career-switchers should look closely too: the bootcamp tradition and beginner-friendly programming across the Futurist family lower the barrier considerably for people early in their web3 journey.

luma-host-evt-S1a3G141Dsg60pk.summaryLead: The Solana Ecosystem Call returns for its August edition - a monthly live show with late-night TV production values, hosted by SOL BROTHERS, drawing over 2,500 registered attendees.

sections.heading: A Crypto Show That Doesn't Feel Like a Crypto Show
content: The Solana Ecosystem Call is pitched as the boldest show in crypto, and the format backs that up. Each monthly episode uses sketches, in-depth interviews, data-driven segments, and unfiltered commentary to break down what matters across the Solana network. It's produced by SOL BROTHERS Studio, which also runs podcasts and host interviews. The production approach borrows from late-night television structure rather than the usual Web3 Twitter space format.

The show is explicitly designed to be cringe-intolerant - a direct contrast to the typical crypto space where someone talks at a static avatar for two hours. SOL BROTHERS bring actual production quality: edited segments, multiple hosts with real chemistry, and a commitment to making the content watchable beyond the core audience. Each episode covers sketches that break down complex topics, interviews with people doing the actual work, and unfiltered takes on what's working and what isn't.

SOL BROTHERS have built their studio around producing content that serves the Solana ecosystem specifically. Their YouTube and X channels host the full archive of past episodes, along with additional podcast content and host interviews. The studio's focus on Solana means they understand the ecosystem deeply enough to ask the right questions and push back when answers feel vague.

sections.heading: How the Community Feeds Into the Show
content: The Ecosystem Call isn't a one-way broadcast. Teams and projects can submit announcements, product launches, event promotions, and giveaway proposals through a public submission form on Linktree. The producers then curate what makes it onto the show, which means the content reflects what the community actually cares about rather than what a marketing team wants to push.

With 2,555 people registered for the August call, the show has become a genuine community gathering point. The hosts include the Solana Foundation, Eno, and Simon Molitor, giving it institutional backing while keeping the personalities front and center. The registration numbers suggest this is one of the larger regular virtual events in the Solana ecosystem, and the curated submission process keeps the quality bar consistent across episodes.

Solana itself is described as a high performance network powering internet capital markets, payments, AI agents, and crypto applications. The ecosystem call translates that technical breadth into digestible segments, helping people understand how different parts of the network connect and where the most interesting activity is happening.

sections.heading: Where to Watch and How to Get Involved
content: The August call is virtual, starting at 10:00 AM Pacific on Wednesday, August 27. Registration is free through Luma, and you can also watch directly on the ecosystemcall.com website. SOL BROTHERS maintains active YouTube and X channels for replays and announcements, so if you miss the live show, you can catch the recording within a reasonable window.

If you're building something on Solana and want exposure to a large, engaged audience, submitting to the show is worth the effort. The audience skews toward people who are already deep in the ecosystem, so you're reaching actual users and potential collaborators rather than passive spectators. The submission process is straightforward, and the producers are selective - getting featured carries more weight than a random tweet thread.

The show was featured in Superteam's programming, which adds another layer of community endorsement. For teams launching new products or protocols on Solana, timing a submission to coincide with the monthly Ecosystem Call can generate meaningful visibility. It's not a silver bullet, but it puts your work in front of thousands of people who are already paying attention to what's moving in the ecosystem.

luma-evt-Dd3eNd55rFmR8bj.summaryLead: A multi-day beginner acting workshop at HAFA Art Studio in Fountain Valley covering camera and theater fundamentals, scene study, and character development - culminating in a certificate and potential casting opportunities.

sections.heading: What the Workshop Covers
content: This is a beginner-level acting workshop spread across six days, totaling 24 hours of instruction. The curriculum is split between acting for camera and acting for theater - two disciplines that share a root but demand very different skills. You'll work through scene study and character development, which means understanding how to break down a script, find a character's motivation, and deliver a performance that feels grounded rather than theatrical.

The workshop is a joint presentation by three organizations: HAFA Art Studio, Starz Studio by Marwa Gabriel, and I Studio by Rafik El Rihany. The involvement of the Hollywood Arab Film Festival/Association (HAFA) as the hosting body connects this workshop to a broader network in the Arab film community. That connection pays off at the end - participants will be considered for future casting opportunities through Starz by Marwa Gabriel, giving the training a direct pathway to professional work.

sections.heading: The Schedule and Where It Happens
content: The workshop runs from September 14 through September 19, 2026. Monday through Friday sessions run from 6:00 PM to 10:00 PM, and Saturday wraps up with an 11:00 AM to 3:00 PM session. That structure lets working people attend the evening sessions without quitting their day jobs, while the Saturday session provides a natural closing experience. The evening format also mirrors real-world filming and rehearsal schedules, which tend to run late - getting used to performing after a full day of other activities is a useful skill in itself.

All sessions take place at HAFA Art Studio, located at 18386 Brookhurst Street in Fountain Valley, California (ZIP code 92708). Fountain Valley sits in Orange County, about 35 miles southeast of downtown Los Angeles. The studio setting means a more intimate learning environment compared to a large theater or university classroom. For beginners who might feel intimidated by a big institutional space, a studio environment tends to feel more personal and less like you're being graded.

sections.heading: Language and Accessibility
content: The instruction is delivered in English with Arabic support available. That bilingual approach reflects the workshop's roots in the Arab film community and makes the training accessible to a wider range of participants. For Arabic-speaking aspiring actors in Southern California, this removes a significant barrier that often exists in English-dominant acting programs.
Every participant who completes the workshop receives a Certificate of Completion presented by all three partner organizations.

sections.heading: Registration, Pricing, and What to Know Before You Sign Up
content: Registration comes with two pricing tiers. Early Bird through August 16 costs $400, and regular registration from August 17 through September 14 is $600. Both tiers are non-refundable and non-transferable, so make sure the dates work before committing. At the time of listing, 14 people were registered and only 2 spots remained. The sharp price jump between early and regular registration - a 50 percent increase - makes a clear case for committing early if you know this is something you want to do.

Spots are filled on a first-come, first-served basis with no waitlist mentioned, which means when they're gone, they're gone. If you're considering this workshop, the early bird pricing saves you $200 and disappears a month before the workshop starts. The combination of 24 hours of instruction, a certificate from three studios, and a pathway to casting considerations makes the $400 early bird price a strong value for serious beginners. For context, a single private acting lesson in Los Angeles typically runs $75 to $150 per hour, so getting 24 hours of group instruction with three studio partners for $400 is a different proposition entirely.

luma-evt-aQiimIN6V6gLF9o.summaryLead: A three-hour program at MIT exploring how AI is reshaping cinema - featuring curated film screenings, filmmaker discussions, industry panels, and networking in Cambridge, Massachusetts on Halloween night.

sections.heading: What This Festival Is
content: The Boston - Silicon Valley AI Film Festival is an extension of an international platform dedicated to the intersection of artificial intelligence and filmmaking. This regional edition, scheduled for October 31, 2026, brings together filmmakers, AI creators, tech innovators, researchers, startup founders, investors, students, and creative professionals for a focused three-hour program at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

The event is hosted by Boston International Media Consulting, Inc. (BIMC), and co-hosted by two MIT student organizations: the Asian Women Development Association (AWDA) and Asian Women Development Plan International (AWDPI). The partnership between a media consulting firm and two MIT student associations reflects the event's dual nature - it's both an industry gathering and an academic exploration of where AI-powered storytelling is heading.

sections.heading: The Program Breakdown
content: The three-hour structure is packed. It opens with remarks, then moves into a curated showcase of AI-assisted and AI-generated films. This isn't a free-for-all screening - the films are selected, which means a curatorial team has decided what's worth showing and in what order. After the showcase, the format shifts to industry panels and roundtable discussions with filmmakers and technology professionals.

An audience Q&A gives attendees direct access to the people making and thinking about AI film. There are also creative-technology presentations or demonstrations, which could range from live AI filmmaking tools to behind-the-scenes looks at production workflows. The program closes with structured networking, giving the 35+ registered attendees a chance to connect with each other and with the featured speakers.

sections.heading: The Topics on the Table
content: The festival explicitly covers a wide range of topics that reflect where the AI-film conversation currently sits. Generative AI and visual storytelling is the big umbrella, but underneath that are more specific threads: AI filmmaking tools and production workflows, emerging video-generation technologies, the tension between human creativity and machine-assisted creation, and the thorny questions around authorship, intellectual property, and responsible AI use.

There's also attention paid to entrepreneurship and innovation in creative technology, plus cross-cultural storytelling in the AI era. That last topic connects to the co-hosts' focus and the international scope of the broader Silicon Valley AI Film Festival.

sections.heading: The Venue and Logistics
content: The event takes place at MIT's campus at 77 Massachusetts Avenue in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The exact room within MIT hasn't been announced yet - registration details and the specific location are noted as forthcoming. The timing on October 31 puts it in the middle of Tough Tech Week, a detail the listing highlights. That scheduling positions the festival within a broader ecosystem of technology and innovation events happening around Boston that week.

The event runs from 2:00 to 5:00 PM EDT, which is early enough that you still have your Halloween evening free. At the time of writing, 35 people were registered as going, with names like Herve Flutto from Sparksense and Prajakta Kalbande among them. Registration is currently open with no mention of a fee, though that could change as the event approaches.

sections.heading: Who Should Show Up
content: This event is most valuable for people who sit at the intersection of film and technology - not just filmmakers curious about AI, and not just technologists curious about film, but people who are actively working at that boundary. If you're building AI tools for video, making films that use generative technology, researching the ethical implications, or investing in creative tech startups, this room has something for you.

The MIT location also makes it accessible to students and researchers who might not have the budget for expensive industry conferences but want to engage with the AI-film conversation. The networking component, with 35+ attendees and panel participants from Sparksense and other organizations, provides the kind of face-to-face connection that's hard to replicate online. And it's free - or at least it's listed without a fee at this stage.

luma-evt-SN7UWBBLgEM1tmn.summaryLead: A $10 Women of Customer Success event in Austin exploring how the Forward Deployed Engineer role is reshaping Customer Success, featuring panel discussions and roundtable conversations with Cloudflare participation.

sections.heading: The Shift Being Examined
content: WoCS Austin X Cloudflare: The Forward Deployed Era + CS's Shift to Revenue takes place Wednesday, September 24, 2026, from 6:30 PM to 9:30 PM in Austin, Texas. The event, priced at $10, addresses a structural change happening across tech organizations: the emergence of the Forward Deployed Engineer role and how it is pulling technical implementation work away from Customer Success Managers.

The core question is what happens to the CSM role when hands-on technical delivery moves to a dedicated function. The event argues that the CSM seat is not disappearing - it is being redefined around a different core skill: owning revenue. This is not a theoretical discussion. The description notes that this shift is happening industry-wide, and the evening is designed for CS professionals who need to understand what it means for their careers.

sections.heading: The Format and What You Get
content: The evening moves from a panel discussion into small-group roundtable conversations. The panel features leaders and practitioners who have lived through this restructuring firsthand, including, if confirmed, a Cloudflare team member in a Forward Deployed Engineer or Solutions seat. Having someone from Cloudflare - a company that has been vocal about its Forward Deployed approach - in the room gives attendees a concrete example of what this role looks like in practice.

The roundtable portion is where the real work happens. Attendees break into small groups to discuss where they personally sit in this shift, what they should hand off, what they should hold onto, and how to build the language and instincts of someone who owns a revenue number. Bites and beverages are provided, keeping the atmosphere social while the content stays substantive. The combination of panel and roundtable means you leave with both big-picture understanding and specific, personal next steps.

sections.heading: Who Should Attend
content: The event targets four groups: CSMs and Account Managers figuring out what stays on their plate, CS leaders and Directors/VPs who already own or are being asked to own a revenue number, RevOps and CS Ops professionals thinking about team design, and anyone in a post-sales role watching their organization create Forward Deployed Engineer or Solutions Consulting seats. That is a broad but coherent audience - everyone in the room is navigating the same structural shift from a different vantage point.

Women of Customer Success is the organizing community, and the event is built for women working in tech and post-sales roles. WoCS operates with over 10 chapters worldwide, and this Austin edition is part of their broader mission to connect, educate, and empower women in post-sales leadership. The community aspect matters here because the shift being discussed is not just technical - it is career-defining, and having a peer group navigating the same transition adds a support layer that a generic tech event would not provide.

sections.heading: Why This Conversation Is Timely
content: The Forward Deployed Engineer role has gained significant traction in recent years, particularly at companies with complex technical products that require hands-on implementation. As these roles proliferate, the boundary between Customer Success and technical delivery is shifting in real time. CSMs who used to own the full post-sales lifecycle - from onboarding through technical setup to ongoing relationship management - are finding that the technical pieces are being peeled off into dedicated functions.

This creates both opportunity and anxiety. Opportunity, because CSMs who can own revenue and drive expansion are more strategically valuable than ever. Anxiety, because the skills that defined a successful CSM - technical knowledge, product expertise, hands-on implementation ability - are being redistributed. The WoCS Austin event addresses both sides of that equation, giving attendees a framework for understanding where the role is heading and what they need to build toward over the next year to stay ahead of the shift.

sections.heading: Why superpollutants matter
content: Beyond Alliance frames this as the first summit of its kind: a dedicated day for senior stakeholders to align on superpollutants rather than treating them as a footnote in broader climate talks. The emphasis is on gases that shape warming over the next few decades—methane, black carbon, nitrous oxide (N₂O), and hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs)—where faster action can change outcomes on a shorter clock than CO₂ alone.

The Luma listing argues that deep reductions over the next ten years could materially bend the warming curve before mid-century. That makes superpollutant mitigation one of the most immediate levers organizers highlight, alongside cleaner air and health gains in communities affected by short-lived pollutants.

sections.heading: Corporate and public momentum
content: Organizers point to rising activity across governments, companies, and civil society—from the Global Methane Pledge to newer corporate commitments. One example on the page is the Superpollutant Action Initiative: a $100 million effort backed by Amazon, Autodesk, Figma, Google, JPMorgan Chase, Salesforce, and Workday to fund high-impact mitigation projects, coordinated by Beyond Alliance.

The audience target is explicit: more than 150 decision-makers working on climate across business, finance, policy, and innovation. The day is built for people who can move capital, set policy, or implement corporate supply-chain and market mechanisms—not a general-audience expo format.

sections.heading: Program themes
content: Session topics listed on Luma include corporate Scope 3 action, emerging market mechanisms, voluntary carbon markets, and the policies and financing needed to scale solutions. The tone is candid dialogue and real commitments rather than keynote-only marketing.

The published agenda shape includes plenary conversations where science, policy, and capital meet, thematic breakouts, a focus on financing faster action at scale, and a showcase of solutions from innovators and project developers on the ground.
